scope: Read-only review of the D1 alias invalidation precision fix in analysis.py and regressions in test_ipc_data_flow_rules.py, especially whether deferral creates false-safe results.
verdict: The unused-local-alias false-positive fix works, but a high-confidence false-safe remains: memcpy-family destination writes through a tracked request pointer alias are exempted from mutation invalidation.

findings.summary: The memcpy-family value API exemption skips writes through request-derived pointer aliases.
findings.detail: value_apis includes policy.copy_calls, then may_mutate is false for an unresolved memcpy/memmove/memcpy_s/memmove_s even when argument 0 is a tracked writable pointer alias. Repro: `int n=data.ReadInt32(); if(n<=0)return -1; char *dst=new char[n]; int *p=&n; int replacement=100; memcpy(p,&replacement,sizeof(n)); const char *src=data.ReadBuffer(n); memcpy(dst,src,n);`. This writes replacement into n through p, so the final copy length no longer has the proven allocation capacity/nonnegative bound. Yet rules_for returns an empty set. Invalidate request aliases for the destination argument of copy-family calls (and separately model source/read-only positions as appropriate) rather than exempting the whole call by name.
findings.reproduction_result: rules_for returned set() for the unsafe sequence above.

fixed_positive_cases: unused writable pointer alias no longer reports ipc.parcel.copy-range
unused writable reference alias no longer reports ipc.parcel.copy-range
negative_cases: unknown call with local reference alias still reports ipc.parcel.copy-range
unknown call with local pointer alias still reports ipc.parcel.copy-range
